A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViPO study and contain readable main text, equations, Figures 1-10, Tables 1-6, and Appendices A-C. Textual and visual inspection supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original image and video generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, qualitative results, and computational overhead measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental outcomes, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations, and supplementary efficiency and VBench results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A and C retain the same PSM, perceptual backbones, allocation maps, advantage weighting, optimization objective, and sampling procedure. Figure 1's edits do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use HPD image prompts and VidProM video prompts, with the same human-preference evaluations, out-of-domain metrics, and redness-reward scenario. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Flux, Wan2.1, DanceGRPO, and the same ablation variants. The newly cited AI Flow and TeleBoost works are not introduced as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same 3,200 image and 1,000 video test prompts, model configurations, resolutions, sampling steps, reward models, evaluation metrics, and training settings.

E4.justification: The backbone comparisons, allocation and aggregation ablations, PCA and smoothing sensitivity studies, redness-reward tests, allocation-map visualizations, and overhead analysis are unchanged, including their supplementary evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting without adding repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Appendix C's shared-initialization-noise statement is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-6 and the experimental comparisons in Figures 3-10 retain the same values and findings. Figure 1's revised overview illustration uses the flower example already present in Figure 7, rather than introducing a new experimental finding.

T1.justification: Equations 1-14 and their mathematical explanations are unchanged, including the GRPO and SDE formulations, perceptual-map construction, and structured-advantage objective. No assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about perceptual credit allocation, compatibility, computational efficiency, and improved image and video generation.

C2.justification: The explanations of region-aware optimization, backbone differences, semantic preservation, and PCA and smoothing tradeoffs are unchanged. No substantive applicability boundary, failure condition, or limitation is added.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information remains unchanged, including backbone feature extraction, GPU counts, learning rates, noise parameters, clipping, timestep fractions, and frame sampling. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v4 adds AI Flow: Perspectives, Scenarios, and Approaches and TeleBoost to the introduction's background citations and bibliography. Existing cited works are retained, and the substantive related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Figure 1 corrects 'Group Relevant Policy Optimization' to 'Group Relative Policy Optimization.' Citation numbering, the version header, and VAST's bibliographic formatting change, while prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces dancing-doll imagery with flower imagery while retaining its diagram structure. Its unchanged caption still refers to the dancing doll. The bibliography reflows; the remaining figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The method, empirical support, analyses, and reproducibility remain unchanged. Correcting the GRPO label and adding two background references provide small editorial benefits, while Figure 1's replacement imagery introduces a mismatch with its unchanged dancing-doll caption. These limited changes do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
